annotation.title_clean: UN Regulation No 155 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regards to cybersecurity and cybersecurity management system [2021/387]
annotation.title_en: UN Regulation No 155 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regards to cybersecurity and cybersecurity management system
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) WP.29; published in Official Journal of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union L 82/30
annotation.summary_en: UNECE WP.29 Regulation No 155, as published in the EU Official Journal, sets uniform type-approval requirements for vehicle cybersecurity. Manufacturers need a certified Cybersecurity Management System and must carry out risk assessment and apply mitigations across the vehicle lifecycle. It covers categories M, N and O vehicles, plus L6/L7 vehicles with Level 3+ automated driving.
key_provisions_or_claims: Vehicle type approval requires a valid Certificate of Compliance for the Cybersecurity Management System (CSMS), valid for up to three years
Manufacturers must run an exhaustive risk assessment considering the Annex 5 threats and apply proportionate mitigations
Continual monitoring, detection of and response to cyberattacks, plus data forensic capability, while respecting privacy and consent
Annual reporting to the approval authority on monitoring outcomes and new cyberattacks
Approval authorities share their assessment methods via the UNECE DETA database to keep application consistent across contracting parties
